catalogMeta.label: Build a Paragraph (open build)
catalogMeta.description: Open build, on the live tutor: tap sentence cards into a paragraph in order: the topic sentence first, two or more facts that belong (any order), the closing last, leaving out the two facts about a different topic. Many paragraphs pass. Checked in code from the cards' roles. Organization only; the writing modes judge no sentence. Beta = informational + 0.1.

cards.text: Sea turtles are reptiles that swim.
They have hard protective shells.
They lay eggs on sandy beaches.
Their front flippers work like paddles.
They eat jellyfish and sea grass.
Sharks have sharp rows of teeth.
Crabs walk sideways on the sand.
Now you know about sea turtles.
Octopuses are clever sea animals.
They have eight long bendy arms.
They squirt dark ink to hide.
Their bodies can quickly change color.
They have three pumping hearts.
Dolphins breathe air through blowholes.
Starfish have tiny tube feet.
That is why octopuses are neat.
Dolphins are smart mammals in oceans.
They swim together in big pods.
They make clicking sounds to talk.
They leap high out of water.
Mother dolphins feed their babies milk.
Seals rest on cold ice sheets.
Eels hide inside dark rocky holes.
Dolphins are wonderful ocean animals.
